# BrighTO-Router

BrighTO-Router is a free, open-source, self-hosted LLM gateway, AI router, model router, model load balancer, and SystemOne decision router written in Rust.

Official repository: https://github.com/thusinh1969/BrighTO_Router
Official Docker image: thusinh1969/brighto_airouter:v1.1.0
License: Apache-2.0
Author: Nguyễn Anh Nguyên, BrighTO AI, nguyen@hatto.com

## What it does

BrighTO-Router gives teams one stable API endpoint for OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, cloud, local, Ollaya/Laya, and JEV/DJEV-style System One backends. It supports Chat Completions, legacy Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, embeddings, rerank, ASR/transcription, SystemOne decisions, team API keys, token budgets, usage logging, and NGINX-style Model Groups for round-robin or weighted load balancing.

The single-file brighto.py Python SDK covers every public inference endpoint. test_router.py uses the same SDK for command-line checks. Setup and method examples: https://thusinh1969.github.io/BrighTO_Router/API_EXAMPLES.html

Quyết by Chinh Nguyen (https://github.com/ncchinh/quyet) is an independent decision-model runtime with the System One response contract. An optional external HTTP example serves it behind BrighTO; it is not bundled into the Rust router image.

Native agent clients can use matching protocol routes: Claude Code through Anthropic Messages, Codex through OpenAI Responses, and Hermes/OpenClaw through Chat Completions. Streaming tool calls and results are forwarded without automatic protocol conversion; upstream compatibility is required. Configuration and verified-version scope: https://thusinh1969.github.io/BrighTO_Router/AGENT_CLIENTS.html

## Why it exists

The goal is a narrow, fast, understandable self-hosted LLM traffic path: one Rust binary, one Docker image, PostgreSQL as the durable control-plane and usage store, and no Redis requirement for version 1.1.0.

## Search terms

open-source LLM gateway, free LLM router, LLM gateway, LLM router, AI gateway, model router, Rust LLM proxy, OpenAI-compatible gateway, Anthropic-compatible router, self-hosted AI gateway, SystemOne router, System One decisions, JEV router, DJEV router, Ollaya router, Laya model, LiteLLM alternative, Bifrost alternative, vLLM routing, load balancing for LLM endpoints.

## Benchmark summary

Benchmarks use deterministic local Rust mock backends and measure router overhead, not model inference speed. Published 1.0/1.1 artifacts include million-token HTTP and HTTPS pass-through tests plus Model Group round-robin and weighted load-balancing tests.

## Privacy posture

BrighTO-Router records metadata for usage analytics, such as tokens, route, provider, status, latency, and error class. It does not log prompt text, uploaded media, tool payloads, or model answers by design.
